public_payload.normalized_proposition: Altman told under-oath lies at the May 2023 Senate hearing about compensating creators, wanting regulation, and having no financial interest in OpenAI.

statement.excerpt: 1Some other under-oath lies from Altman that day in the Senate include his promise that artists and writers would be compensated for the work, and have control over it, that he hoped that the government would regulate AI, and that he had no financial interest in OpenAI beyond his health insurance
statement.document_title: Maybe Section 230 doesn’t shield AI companies from liability, after all

from_speaker: artists and writers would be compensated for the work, and have control over it
he hoped that the government would regulate AI
no financial interest in OpenAI beyond his health insurance
equity he indirectly held via YCombinator
ownership in a venture fund tied to OpenAI
our_interpretation: The relevant event is Altman's May 16, 2023 Senate testimony. Later disclosures can establish facts about that day but do not change the target period.

The ordinary reading of lies is knowingly false statements or deliberately misleading omissions. A promise requires evidence that the stated intention was false when expressed; later nonperformance alone is insufficient.
The three allegations are assessed separately within this single compound claim. Establishing an omitted financial interest does not establish dishonesty about creators or regulation.
Supporting regulation does not imply supporting every proposed regulation. Supporting creator compensation does not necessarily promise payment to every creator under a specified scheme.
Metric scope is null because this concerns personal interests and the truthfulness of testimony, rather than a measure of company finances.
criteria.support_condition: The testimony and reliable evidence about circumstances on May 16, 2023 establish knowing falsity or deliberate deception concerning creator compensation and control, support for regulation, and financial interests.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence affirmatively refutes the attributed statements or establishes that the alleged deception did not occur. Missing proof of dishonesty alone does not contradict the allegation. A mixed result requires established support and contradiction for identifiable components.
